title: BCCI vice-president praises Sonal Dinusha for consistent form in Colombo Test series
byline: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) vice-president Rajeev Shukla has commended Sri Lankan batter Sonal Dinusha for his consistent performances against India in the ongoing Test series. Shukla described Dinusha as a potential great in Test cricket and remarked that he “looks like Tendulkar”.

title: Uefa pursuing criminal legal action against Infantino
byline: Uefa is pursuing criminal legal proceedings against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over the now scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and its other competitions to private investors.

title: Couple arrested with Rs. 70 mn worth of heroin, ‘Ice’ in Matara
byline: A married couple allegedly involved in drug trafficking was arrested in Matara today (27) after police uncovered a large consignment of heroin and ‘Ice’ during a raid on a beauty salon.

title: Dinusha leads Sri Lanka’s epic resistance in a gritty draw
byline: A third hundred in four innings from the unstoppable Sonal Dinusha led Sri Lanka to an epic draw in the second Test at the SSC, with the lower order supporting him doggedly through a fifth day of intense toil for India’s bowlers. By the time the teams shook hands, Sri Lanka had made India bowl 243.4 overs across back-to-back innings, having enforced the follow-on.

title: President pays homage to Sacred Tooth Relic
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, who is in Kandy to participate in the annual Esala Perahera celebrations, paid homage to the Sacred Tooth Relic at the historic Sri Dalada Maligawa this afternoon (27).

title: BASL calls for responsible scrutiny of Judiciary amid 22nd Amendment concerns
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has called for a responsible scrutiny of the Judiciary while reiterating its opposition to the proposed Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution, citing concerns over judicial independence and the rights and interests of the people.

title: No Sri Lankans among tourists reported missing:  Nepal Tourism Board
byline: The Nepal Tourism Board in its latest update said that a total of 644 people are currently reported missing including 127 Nepalese nationals and 517 foreign nationals from 32 countries.

title: NPP MP seeks dismissal of BASL petition on 22nd Amendment
byline: National People’s Power (NPP) Parliamentarian Lakshman Nipuna Arachchi has filed an intervenient petition in the Supreme Court seeking an order to dismiss the Special Determination petition filed by two office-bearers of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) against the proposed Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution.

title: Three killed, including 10-day-old infant, in jeep–three-wheeler collision
byline: Three people, including an infant, died in an accident this morning, involving a collision between a jeep and a three-wheeler in the Gonamariyawa area along the Kebithigollewa  Medawachchiya main road.

title: Gregory Lake water pollution poses serious health risk, CEA finds
byline: Water in Nuwara Eliya’s Gregory Lake has reached a level of pollution that could pose a serious risk to human health if consumed, according to findings presented by the Central Environmental Authority (CEA).

title: Nuwara Eliya lowest, Jaffna, Mannar, Polonnaruwa highest temperature today
byline: Nuwara Eliya recorded Sri Lanka’s lowest minimum temperature of 14.9°C, while the highest minimum temperature of 27°C was recorded in Jaffna, Mannar and Polonnaruwa, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Nearly 1,500 missing in Nepal and China after devastating Himalayan flash flood
byline: Nearly 1,500 people including almost 800 foreigners are missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet, authorities said on Thursday, after a wall of mud ​and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river, sending catastrophic flash floods through towns and valleys.

title: Dengue cases surpass 94,000 as death toll reaches 72
byline: Sri Lanka has recorded 94,666 dengue cases and 72 deaths so far this year, according to the latest dengue surveillance data as of midnight on August 26.

title: Emergency hotlines activated for Sri Lankans in Nepal
byline: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism has activated 24-hour emergency hotlines to provide assistance and coordinate support for Sri Lankan nationals currently in Nepal.

title: Rooftop solar systems over 300kW asked to temporarily halt generation
byline: The National System Operator (Pvt) Ltd has requested the temporary deactivation of rooftop solar power systems with a capacity exceeding 300 kilowatts due to lower electricity demand during the holiday period.

title: Nilaveli coral centre to open as museum and research facility
byline: The Coral Conservation Centre and Laboratory being established in Nilaveli is expected to be developed into a Coral Museum and Research Centre, providing opportunities for university students, researchers and the general public to study Sri Lanka’s marine ecosystems.

title: Vijitha Herath telephones Nepal Foreign Minister; offers support
byline: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said he held a productive call with Nepal’s Foreign Minister, Shisir Khanal, to discuss the current situation following the devastating floods.

title: Meta agrees to pay $18 billion to settle US lawsuits over children’s social media addiction
byline: Meta Platforms will pay up to $18 billion over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram under an agreement with nearly all U.S. states to resolve claims it designed those social media platforms to addict children.

title: Sri Lankan embassy issues urgent safety advisory due to Nepal floods
byline: The Sri Lankan Embassy in Kathmandu has issued an urgent safety advisory to Sri Lankan nationals in Nepal following a sudden flash flood that entered Rasuwa district through the Bhote Koshi River from the Tibetan side.

title: Sri Lanka offers support to Nepal in flood rescue and clearance operations
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said Sri Lanka stands ready to assist Nepal in rescue and clearance operations following the devastating floods.

title: SL ranks 120th among 130 countries in ILO wage study
byline: Sri Lanka stands at 120th among 130 countries surveyed in a global minimum wage comparison published by ’’Visual Capitalist’’ with its purchasing power-adjusted monthly minimum wage estimated at $200.

title: Prison overcrowding to ease in one month: Minister
byline: Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara said yesterday that overcrowding in prisons will be reduced in a month or one and half months as the government has taken steps to expedite issuance of reports by the government Analyst Department.

title: Are Sri Lanka’s wildlife laws enough to stop the destruction of medicinal plants?
byline: Sri Lanka is preparing to mark World Wildlife Day 2026 amid growing concerns over the exploitation of medicinal and aromatic plants, raising questions over whether existing laws and enforcement are strong enough to prevent the country’s valuable biodiversity from being depleted.

title: Pathirage throws 92.07m to win Zurich Diamond League
byline: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage produced another stunning performance, throwing 92.07m to win the men’s javelin at the Zurich Diamond League.

title: Norway’s King Harald dies aged 89
byline: Norway’s King Harald V has died at the age of 89, after he was taken to hospital last week for treatment for a rare blood condition.

title: ’High risk’ of lake breaching and causing second flood, warns China
byline: China has warned there is a ’’high risk’’ that a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.

title: Central Highlands Protection Authority Bill to be presented to Parliament soon: President
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said today that the Bill to establish the Central Highlands Protection Authority is expected to be presented to Parliament for approval by the end of this year or early next year.

title: Pharmacists to launch one-day strike
byline: The Government Pharmacists’ Association has decided to launch a one-day strike from 8 a.m. on August 31, citing unresolved issues over the “additional service allowance” paid to pharmacists.

title: 245 coral species identified along Sri Lanka’s Eastern coast
byline: A total of 245 coral species have been identified along Sri Lanka’s eastern coastline, highlighting the importance of protecting the country’s diverse marine ecosystems.

title: Over 200 jumbos perish in eight months
byline: More than 200 wild elephants have died in Sri Lanka during the first eight months of 2026, according to the Department of Wildlife Conservation.

title: Youth arrested for whipping pony near Lake Gregory
byline: A 26-year-old man has been arrested by Nuwara Eliya Police for allegedly assaulting a pony used for tourist rides near Lake Gregory in Nuwara Eliya.

title: Expert highlights hidden holiday risks for children
byline: School holidays provide children with more time to relax and play, but they can also increase their exposure to preventable accidents and illnesses, Consultant Paediatrician Dr. Maheshaka Wijayawardena warned.

title: Missing woman turns up at police station with marriage certificate
byline: A young woman from Pidurupitiya in Monaragala, who had been reported missing from her home for five days, turned up at the Mahakalugolla Police Station and informed police that she had got married.

title: Expressways generate Rs. 124.57m in two days
byline: Country’s expressways generated a total revenue of Rs. 124.57 million from 325,316 vehicles during August 26 and 27, according to the latest expressway revenue figures.

title: Social media groups allegedly used to trade sexual content
byline: Groups operating on Facebook and other social media platforms are allegedly being used to trade sexual videos and private photographs of women and children, raising serious concerns over online exploitation, the Women and Child Affairs Ministry said.

title: Number affected by El Niño climbs to 84,546 as vegetable prices set to rise
byline: The number of people affected by the worsening impact of El Niño conditions has increased to 84,546, raising concerns over a possible surge in vegetable prices in the coming days.

title: Sun directly overhead Sri Lanka till September 7
byline: The sun is expected to be directly overhead in Kokkuvil, Nallur, Kodikamam and Nagar Kovil about 12.11 noon today, the Meteorology Department said.

title: How Sri Lanka can turn resources into riches
byline: Switzerland, a landlocked nation devoid of precious metals or crude oil, stands as one of the world’s richest economies. It thrives on precision machinery, pharmaceuticals, and high-end consumer goods like chocolate and watches, supported by the world’s most trusted banking system. title: Nepal flash flood death toll rises to 469
byline: Rescue teams using heavy machinery dug through mud and debris in Nepalese towns devastated by a flash flood two days ago, as hopes of finding ​survivors faded and officials worked to reduce the risk of further catastrophic flooding.

title: Sri Lanka extends US$ 1 million humanitarian assistance to Nepal
byline: President Anura Kumara Disanayaka has directed the government to provide a financial contribution of US$ 1 million to Nepal to support its ongoing humanitarian and relief efforts, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism said.

title: Two years almost gone; State bungalows await productive use
byline: Despite the lapse of nearly two years, the government is still in the process of converting around 30 state bungalows formerly occupied by Cabinet ministers into productive-use properties, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: Sarath Manamendra files petition in support of 22nd Amendment
byline: Leader of the Nava Sihala Urumaya political party Sarath Manamendra today filed an intervenient petition before the Supreme Court, seeking a determination that the proposed Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution, in its entirety, is not inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution and therefore does not require the approval of the people at a referendum.

title: Urgent action plan launched to tackle pollution in Gregory Lake
byline: Authorities have launched an urgent joint action plan to address the worsening water pollution issue at Gregory Lake in Nuwara Eliya, with immediate and long-term measures proposed to protect the lake and preserve its tourism value.

title: Ugandan King, once world’s youngest monarch, dies at 34
byline: Oyo Nyimba, a Ugandan king, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the crown in 1995, has died aged 34, the prime minister of ​his kingdom announced.

title: Colombo Port rises to 20th among world’s busiest container ports
byline: The Port of Colombo has climbed to 20th place among the world’s major container ports after recording an 11.9 per cent year-on-year increase in container handling during the first half of 2026, according to the latest Alphaliner figures.

title: Former Speaker denies vehicle, fuel misuse allegations
byline: Former Speaker Mahinda Yapa Abeywardena has strongly denied allegations concerning his use of vehicles and fuel during his tenure, claiming that findings of a special audit report are being distorted by certain groups to mislead the public.

title: Brawl erupts at Colombo Divisional Secretariat
byline: A tense situation was reported at the Colombo Divisional Secretariat today after a large crowd became agitated over delays in obtaining copies of birth certificates.

title: Norway’s King Harald dies aged 89
byline: Norway’s King Harald V has died at the age of 89, after he was taken to hospital last week for treatment for a rare blood condition.

title: Growing digital risks raise concerns over child safety
byline: Growing concerns over excessive online gaming, cyberbullying and children’s exposure to online betting are highlighting the need for stronger measures to protect children in Sri Lanka’s increasingly digital environment, psychiatrist Dr. Rumi Ruben said.

title: CSE returns to gains as foreign buying supports a volatile session
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange returned to positive territory on Friday, 28 August 2026, with both benchmark indices closing marginally higher following a volatile trading session and a return of foreign buying.

title: President pledges full rights, better life for Malayagam community
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said the previous Cabinet had decided to remove obstacles faced by people who had left Sri Lanka during the war and were living in India, enabling them to return to the country.

title: India races to Nepal’s aid after deadly floods, sends 62 tonnes of relief
byline: Less than 12 hours after the deadly flash floods hit Nepal on August 26, an Indian Air Force C-130J aircraft took off carrying 10 tonnes of humanitarian and disaster-relief supplies. The first consignment reached Kathmandu later that night.

title: Parliament to convene for four days from September 8
byline: Parliament is scheduled to convene from September 8 to 11, following a decision taken by the Committee on Parliamentary Business.

title: Nearly 500 killed, over 1,400 still missing due to Nepal floods
byline: Devastating floods on the Nepal-China border region this week have killed at least 547 people, Nepal’s police have said.

title: PM Harini hails Vasudeva Nanayakkara’s contribution to Sri Lanka’s left-wing politics
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has described veteran politician and former Parliamentarian Vasudeva Nanayakkara as an important figure in Sri Lanka’s left-wing political history.

title: Drug and alcohol use claims nearly 100 deaths daily in Sri Lanka
byline: Drug and alcohol use is contributing to the deaths of between 80 and 100 people in Sri Lanka every day, according to Dr. Manoj Fernando, Dean of the Faculty of Applied Sciences at Rajarata University.

title: India races to Nepal’s aid after deadly floods, sends 62 tonnes of relief
byline: Less than 12 hours after the deadly flash floods hit Nepal on August 26, an Indian Air Force C-130J aircraft took off carrying 10 tonnes of humanitarian and disaster-relief supplies. The first consignment reached Kathmandu later that night.

byline: Devastating floods on the Nepal-China border region this week have killed at least 547 people, Nepal’s police have said.

byline: Oyo Nyimba, a Ugandan king, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the crown in 1995, has died aged 34, the prime minister of ​his kingdom announced.
